identity.title: An Optimized Franz-Parisi Criterion and its Equivalence with SQ Lower Bounds

problem.claim: Develop a criterion for characterizing computationally hard phases in statistical detection and relate it to SQ lower bounds.

gap.claim: The earlier FP criterion was based on an annealed potential and was shown equivalent to LDP lower bounds for Gaussian additive models; the paper presents this as insufficiently aligned with overlap geometry and seeks a broader connection.

contributions.claim: Proposes a refined, optimized Franz-Parisi criterion intended to better capture the overlap structure of statistical models.
Establishes an equivalence between the optimized FP criterion and SQ lower bounds under a mild, verifiable assumption.
Uses the equivalence to unify and simplify several known SQ lower-bound derivations and to obtain additional lower bounds for mixed sparse linear regression and convex truncation.

stated_novelty.claim: The stated new distinction is an optimized FP criterion equivalent to SQ lower bounds across a broad class of models under a mild assumption.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the equivalence applies to Gaussian additive, planted sparse, NGCA, SI, and convex truncation settings.
For convex truncation, the authors report that the required assumption is equivalent to the Gaussian correlation inequality.
The authors report both simplified derivations of known NGCA and SI SQ lower bounds and new bounds for mixed sparse linear regression and convex truncation.

narrative_sequence.summary: An earlier FP criterion characterized hard phases and connected FP analysis with LDP lower bounds for Gaussian additive models.
The paper refines the criterion to better represent model overlap geometry.
It states equivalence with SQ lower bounds under a mild, verifiable assumption covering several model families.
The equivalence is reported to simplify known derivations and produce new lower bounds in two settings.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a geometric refinement of the criterion with an explicit assumption and then states the model classes covered by that assumption.

lessons.interpretation: This links a conceptual change to a checkable applicability condition, making the scope of the theorem more assessable.
lessons.application: When introducing a theoretical framework, state the structural object being improved, the exact assumption needed, and representative settings where it can be verified.
lessons.exception: This pattern is less suitable when the work is exploratory and no formal applicability condition or model class is yet available.

unknowns: The abstract does not state the formal optimized FP definition or the precise equivalence theorem.
The quantitative form and strength of the reported SQ lower bounds are unspecified.
The assumption’s exact statement and verification details are not provided beyond the convex-truncation connection to the Gaussian correlation inequality.
